understandability.claim: README documents the Minecraft/NeoForge target, build and installation paths, server behavior, configuration, client scanner, privacy and enforcement limits, data-pack extension points, administrator commands, persistence, evidence logs, and security limitations.

verification.claim: The stable candidate records one exact-head gate spanning Build, GameTest, Packaged Server, External Runtime, and Ubuntu/Windows/macOS scanner checks; all required workflows succeeded and all 24 required GameTests passed.

A packaged NeoForge server and real Minecraft protocol client exercised a real block-break packet through BlockEvent.BreakEvent, production warning progression, JSONL evidence logging, and actual connection termination with action=kick.

reproducibility.claim: The build records Java 21, Minecraft 1.21.1, NeoForge 21.1.235, mod version 1.1.0, test dependencies, production/gameTest source separation, and the Gradle build path.

An isolated offline clean build succeeded and produced a JAR byte-for-byte identical to the GitHub-built stable candidate with SHA-256 4cc843c0c39348203e3ffe30ab4dbd6c33a9eb0f6d2907913d005b89a80588fe.

interoperability.claim: The repository defines exact Minecraft/NeoForge compatibility, separate server-only and optional client installation modes, behavior with FakePlayers and tools from other mods, and data-pack tags that other content can extend.

Scanner and recursive filesystem-watcher behavior passed on Ubuntu, Windows, and macOS; this evidence is bounded to scanner/watcher behavior and does not claim a complete graphical Minecraft runtime on all three platforms.

security-safety.claim: The client scanner explicitly documents fail-open/fail-closed policy, high-confidence blocking boundaries, privacy behavior, non-attestation, false-positive limits, and that it is not a tamper-proof or server-enforced anti-cheat.

stewardship.claim: Repository build metadata records MIT licensing and stable version 1.1.0.
The release receipt freezes exact artifact identity and requires publication from the reviewed stable-candidate JAR without rebuilding it after approval.

understandability.claim: The active-carrier README documents the one-realm public-claim model, commands, configuration, personal/public capacity isolation, exact Minecraft/NeoForge/FTB compatibility, automated validation, and the migration boundary for unreleased multi-project development saves.

verification.claim: The exact carrier passed clean Java 21 build and distributable-JAR audit, FTB Chunks client ABI inspection, real Xvfb mouse interaction, combined NeoForge GameTests, and second-JVM dedicated-server persistence validation.
A separate exact-head compatibility run passed compile/test/JAR audit, runtime dependency metadata checks, FTB Chunks 2101.1.21 client-map ABI inspection, and combined NeoForge GameTests.

reproducibility.claim: The exact carrier records Java 21, Minecraft 1.21.1, NeoForge 21.1.242, Architectury 13.0.8, FTB Chunks 2101.1.21 with minimum 2101.1.20, FTB Teams 2101.1.10, FTB Library 2101.1.34, and the Gradle build contract; the clean CI build and distributable-JAR audit succeeded at this revision.

maintainability.claim: Version-sensitive FTB Teams/Chunks integration is isolated behind a dedicated bridge and the README explicitly identifies the compatibility boundary; this supports the bounded architectural claim without asserting broad long-term maintainability for every component.

interoperability.claim: The carrier documents coexistence with BuyClaimChunks Continued, separate personal/public capacity and ownership domains, exact supported FTB ranges, client/server installation requirements, and the verified private-ABI boundary.

The exact head passed the compatible FTB stack with FTB Chunks 2101.1.21, validated runtime dependency metadata and client-map ABI, and ran combined NeoForge GameTests with BuyClaimChunks Continued present.

security-safety.claim: The active carrier documents fail-safe ownership boundaries: public claims do not overwrite personal/party claims, public capacity is isolated, fake-player editing is disabled by default, explosion and mob-grief terrain damage are disabled by default, payload changes are bounded, and legacy multi-team saves are not auto-merged when ownership could conflict.

stewardship.claim: The carrier records MIT licensing, explicit 0.2.0-SNAPSHOT identity, exact compatibility and migration boundaries, and a documented validation contract; the snapshot/draft state is preserved as lifecycle context rather than presented as a stable release.
